second_order.event: US designates helium as critical material
second_order.effect: Accelerates strategic stockpiling and domestic production incentives, benefiting US industrial gas suppliers and semiconductor fabs reliant on helium for cooling
second_order.who_is_affected: US semiconductor manufacturers, industrial gas companies (Air Products, Linde), defense contractors

second_order.event: Bank of Canada projected to raise rates to 2.50% by Oct 28 and again by March
second_order.effect: Tightens Canadian mortgage and corporate borrowing costs just as US tariff relief provides marginal export relief, creating divergent policy pressure on CAD
second_order.who_is_affected: Canadian households, rate-sensitive sectors (real estate, autos), BoC credibility

second_order.event: OpenAI shifts frontier model training offline after cyber incidents
second_order.effect: Signals new security paradigm for AI labs, likely increasing compute costs and slowing iteration cycles for frontier models across the industry
second_order.who_is_affected: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, cloud providers (Azure, AWS), AI safety regulators

contrarian.why_it_matters: Reveals decoupling between primary market euphoria (retail speculation) and secondary market reality (FII selling, global risk-off); potential for post-listing disappointment if macro deteriorates

contrarian.signal: Trump lifts tariffs on some Canadian goods but adds others, net protectionism unchanged
contrarian.mainstream_view: Tariff relief signals de-escalation and Canada-US trade normalization
contrarian.why_it_matters: Product substitution maintains tariff revenue and political leverage; Canadian exporters face continued uncertainty, BoC cannot factor in durable trade improvement

contrarian.signal: Nvidia CEO encourages Europe's 'lagging' AI sector and unveils shipping-container AI factory
contrarian.mainstream_view: Nvidia dominance is unassailable, AI capex boom benefits all semiconductor names equally
contrarian.why_it_matters: Highlights geographic concentration risk (US/China/Taiwan) and form-factor innovation (modular data centers) that could disrupt traditional colocation and cloud models, creating new winners/losers

intelligence.bottom_line: Tonight's defining tension is the collision of a potential US-Iran conflict driving oil to six-month highs with midterm-driven tariff theater that offers Canada only tactical relief. Meanwhile, India's record IPO frenzy masks a brutal secondary market selloff, and the AI capex boom is fracturing into haves (Nvidia, data center builders) and have-nots (software monetization laggards).
